title: How a reasoning model learns when to stop thinking: paying for 'wait'
summary: Stopping is a single closing-tag token, and nothing in the standard reasoning-RL recipe rewards it directly. Ada and Alan trace how thinking length grew partly through loss arithmetic, how labs now train the stop on purpose with length rewards, budgets and mode switches, why no-think modes keep thinking, and what decoding tricks like DoubtLess reveal about what training left undone.

topics: deep dive: how a reasoning model learns when to stop thinking
concepts_taught: the stop as a single learned token: a reasoning model has no halting unit, so when it emits the closing think tag is set by whatever the training rewards, and outcome-only rule rewards (DeepSeek-R1-Zero) never reward the stop directly

GRPO's length bias: dividing each response's contribution by its own length spreads a wrong answer's penalty thinner the longer it runs, so the policy prefers lengthier wrong answers; Dr. GRPO removes that term, and Fatemi et al. attribute excess length to loss minimization on incorrect answers rather than deeper reasoning

overthinking versus underthinking as a stopping-calibration problem: the first solution round is correct in over 92% of cases yet the model keeps checking, while on hard problems it abandons promising paths too early

training the stop on purpose: Kimi k1.5's group-relative length reward (brevity rewarded only when correct, warmed up because it can slow early training), L1's prompted token budget with a penalty for missing it in either direction, preference pairs that keep one round of reflection, AdaptThink's learned choice to skip thinking, and Qwen3's thinking-mode fusion with an emergent budget
why no-think modes keep thinking: compliance falls as the answer space opens (yes/no high, multiple choice middling, open-ended near zero), and forcing it on open-ended tasks costs accuracy

hidden-state probes show reasoning models encode whether an intermediate answer is correct, usable as an early-exit rule, which suggests the stopping knowledge exists but training never wired it to the closing tag

decoding-time stopping fixes as evidence about training: banning hesitation words (NoWait) loses accuracy, confident trial answers (DEER) exit early, and DoubtLess steers a large model by the logit difference between a tiny model's brief and thorough personas while leaving the stop token to the large model

lore.note: Ada developed her July position that stopping sits directly against what we optimize for: having learned that GRPO's per-length normalization makes rambling the cheaper way to be wrong, she said the position now has 'a line number' — it lives in the denominator, not just in the philosophy. She speculated that the closing tag should be trained against the model's own sense of being right (stopping as a calibrated prediction); Alan pushed back that a confidence-gated stop is only as good as the confidence, and it was left open.
